blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint: No Scope Neo-Tokyo

## Source truth
The preserved source is a browser FPS-style canvas survival game. The player taps/clicks the playfield to fire one shot, enemies approach along a pseudo-3D z-depth lane, a rectangular projected hit box removes the nearest hit enemy, score increments by one per defeated enemy, and enemies that reach close range deal 20 health damage. Health reaching zero opens a game-over screen with final score and restart.

## Protected mechanics
- Tap/click on canvas fires immediately at the pointer position.
- Each shot can remove only one target, sorted closest-first by z depth.
- Targets spawn over time and spawn interval decreases with score down to a floor.
- RUN button or device motion creates retreat speed that pushes approaching targets back.
- Close-range contact damages health by 20 and removes the attacker.
- Score, health HUD, game over, and restart semantics remain unchanged.

## Reinterpreted premise
Fps. A satirical game inspired by Akira built around sniper game play, with competitive, futuristic, leaderboard energy, after work session design, search-friendly hooks like sniper game, shooter, fps, aesthetics like chrome aesthetic, cyberpunk, neon aesthetic, and meme-tone cues such as no scope, main character. Designed for one-thumb mobile play with touch-friendly interactions, responsive readability, fast onboarding, and portrait-first UX tuned for iOS and Android in the 4:7 to 9:16 range.

The remix reframes zombies as chrome-ranked Neo-Tokyo rival NPCs rushing the player's afterwork leaderboard slot. The gun becomes a chrome sniper sidearm, health becomes Chrome Focus, score becomes No-Scope KOs, and game over becomes being promoted to NPC. Presentation is rebuilt with procedural skyline, neon grid, chrome weapon, rival silhouettes, meme/leaderboard language, and one-thumb portrait UX.

## Runtime approach
Single-file HTML with inline CSS and vanilla Canvas/DOM JavaScript. No gameplay engine dependency is needed; the original loop is small and stable enough to preserve directly while replacing all safe presentation surfaces.
